question.text: A 60/40 portfolio after 1 year of strong equity (+25%, bonds 0%). Post-drift equity weight is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Starting weights are equity 60 and bonds 40 (total 100). After one year, equity grows 25% to 60 × 1.25 = 75; bonds stay at 40. New total = 75 + 40 = 115. Equity weight = 75 / 115 ≈ 65.2%, closest to 65%. The Trap: 60% ignores the drift entirely. 70% and 75% overstate the drift — note that bonds at 40 dilute the new equity share so the weight rises only to about 65%, not all the way to 75%.
